full_text_en:
Shi Feng Technology Co., Ltd. v. Fujun New Composite Materials (Taicang) Co., Ltd., and Third Party Winning Group Limited — Dispute over Company Dissolution

【Ruling Summary】

1. Article 183 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China serves both as a condition for accepting a company dissolution lawsuit and as a substantive condition for adjudicating company dissolution. Whether a company should be dissolved depends on whether a deadlock exists and whether the substantive conditions under Article 183 of the Company Law are satisfied, and not on the cause or fault leading to the deadlock. Even if one shareholder is at fault in causing the company deadlock, that shareholder is still entitled to bring a company dissolution lawsuit. A lawsuit brought by a fault-bearing shareholder should not be automatically equated with malicious litigation.

2. A company deadlock does not necessarily lead to dissolution. The judiciary should exercise caution in intervening in corporate affairs. Where there are other means to maintain the company's existence, the company should not be readily dissolved. Where a company falls into a persistent deadlock, all other means have been exhausted without resolution, and the company is no longer viable for continued operations, and continued existence will cause significant harm to shareholders' interests, the court may order the dissolution of the company in accordance with Article 183 of the Company Law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 29

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Fujun New Composite Materials (Taicang) Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 88, Hufu Huang Highway, Fuqiao Town, Taicang City, Jiangsu Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Huang Chongsheng, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Bao Zhonghua, lawyer of Jiangsu Jintai Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): SHIN FENG TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. Domicile: OFFSHORE CHAMBERS, P.O. BOX 217, APIA, SAMOA.

Legal Representative: Zheng Ping, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yu Yunbin, lawyer of Beijing Fada Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Boqin, male, born on October 23, 1965, a resident of Kaohsiung City, Taiwan region, currently residing at No. 8, Qiangjin Street, Jibei Economic Development Zone, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Third Party at First Instance: WINNING GROUP LIMITED. Domicile: OFFSHORE CHAMBERS, P.O. BOX 217, APIA, SAMOA.

Legal Representative: Huang Chongsheng, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Cao Quannan, lawyer of Jiangsu Jintai Law Firm.

The appellant, Fujun New Composite Materials (Taicang) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fujun Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2007) Su Min San Chu Zi No. 3 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court on May 26, 2011, in a dispute over company dissolution with the respondent, Shi Feng Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shi Feng Company), and the third party at first instance, Winning Group Limited (hereinafter referred to as Winning Company), to this court. After accepting the case, this court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of trial judge Chen Jizhong as presiding judge, trial judge Gao Xiaoli, and acting trial judge Shen Hongyu, and held a public hearing on October 27, 2011. The court clerk Zhang Bona recorded the proceedings. The following persons appeared in court: Bao Zhonghua, agent ad litem of appellant Fujun Company; Zhu Xiaobo and Zhu Lei, former agents ad litem of respondent Shi Feng Company; and Cao Quannan, agent ad litem of third party at first instance Winning Company. On March 22, 2012, this court received a power of attorney sent by Shi Feng Company from abroad, which had been duly notarized and authenticated, terminating the authorization of Zhu Xiaobo and Zhu Lei and reappointing Yu Yunbin and Zhang Boqin as agents ad litem of the company. This case is now concluded.

Shi Feng Company filed a complaint with the court of first instance, alleging: The registered capital of Fujun Company was USD 10 million, with Winning Company holding 40% of the capital contribution and Shi Feng Company holding 60%. On April 28, 2004, in the absence of Shi Feng Company, Winning Company forged the signatures of Shi Feng Company's directors, fabricated a board resolution, unilaterally amended the articles of association, stipulating that "the chairman shall be appointed by Party B (i.e., Winning Company)", and submitted false materials for approval and registration. Through fraudulent means, Winning Company enabled its appointed director Huang Chongsheng to "legitimately" control Fujun Company through the position of chairman, ousting Shi Feng Company's appointed director from Fujun Company, and engaging in malicious transactions with its affiliated companies, seriously harming the interests of the major shareholder of Fujun Company. Fujun Company had not convened a board meeting for a long time, failed to inform Shi Feng Company of its operations and financial status, and Winning Company refused Shi Feng Company's reasonable requests to rectify the corporate governance structure. As a shareholder, Shi Feng Company's rights to asset returns, participation in major decisions, and selection of managers were completely frustrated. Shi Feng Company argued that the conflicts and tensions between shareholders of Fujun Company had rendered the company's operational mechanism completely dysfunctional. The board of directors, as the authority body, could not make any decisions on any matters of Fujun Company. The company's operations were deadlocked, and its management encountered severe difficulties, causing serious harm to the legitimate interests of Fujun Company and its major shareholder. This fell within the circumstances stipulated in Article 183 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law). It requested the court to order the dissolution of Fujun Company and that Fujun Company bear the litigation costs.

Fujun Company argued in its defense: The allegations by Shi Feng Company that Winning Company forged director signatures and fabricated board resolutions were not true. After Winning Company and Shi Feng Company cooperated to establish Fujun Company, the actual operations were conducted by Zhang Boqin, the director appointed by Shi Feng Company. Huang Chongsheng, though chairman, did not participate in management. On April 7, 2005, Zhang Boqin left his post without authorization, and Huang Chongsheng took over management and has managed the company since then. Huang Chongsheng had repeatedly requested Shi Feng Company to send its appointed director Zhang Boqin back to perform his duties and convene a board meeting, but Zhang Boqin never returned to fulfill his obligations at Fujun Company. The inability to convene board meetings and the conflicts among shareholders were caused by Shi Feng Company. Fujun Company had not reached a deadlock, let alone severe management difficulties. The company had been operating normally and with good development momentum. In Shandong Province, Zhang Boqin, the director appointed by Shi Feng Company, had established Jinan Tongyi Energy-Saving Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tongyi Company), which produced the same products as Fujun Company. The purpose of Shi Feng Company's lawsuit was to dissolve Fujun Company in order to allow Tongyi Company to monopolize the market. It requested the court to dismiss Shi Feng Company's claims.

Winning Company submitted its statement: It agreed with the arguments of Fujun Company.

The court of first instance found the following facts through trial: On November 27, 2002, PEREZ LIMITED, a company incorporated in Samoa, established a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, Beikelai New Composite Materials (Taicang) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beikelai Company), with a registered capital of USD 1.05 million. On April 28, 2004, because the shareholder's capital contribution had not been fully paid, Beikelai Company passed a board resolution to transfer all shares of the company to Winning Company and to accept Shi Feng Company as an investor of Beikelai Company with additional investment; it reappointed Huang Chongsheng as chairman of Beikelai Company, and Zheng Sulan and Zhang Boqin as directors; it also required amendments to the articles of association, which, after confirmation by the investors, should be submitted to the original approval authority for approval and registration.

The articles of association of Beikelai Company as recorded in the industrial and commercial registration on April 28, 2004, stated: Winning Company and Shi Feng Company jointly invested in Beikelai Company with additional investment. After the additional investment, the registered capital of the company was USD 10 million, of which Winning Company contributed USD 4 million (USD 400,000 in cash and machinery and equipment valued at USD 3.6 million), accounting for 40% of the capital contribution, and Shi Feng Company contributed USD 6 million (USD 600,000 in cash and machinery and equipment valued at USD 5.4 million), accounting for 60% of the capital contribution. Article 17 of the articles of association provided that the company shall establish a board of directors, which is the highest authority of the company. Article 21 provided that the board of directors shall consist of three directors, with two appointed by Shi Feng Company and one appointed by Winning Company, and the chairman shall be appointed by Winning Company. Article 23 provided that the board of directors shall hold regular meetings and interim meetings, with regular meetings to be held within the year-end period and interim meetings to be held when deemed necessary. Article 24 provided that board meetings shall be convened and presided over by the chairman, and in the absence of the chairman, a representative appointed by the chairman may preside. Article 25 provided that board meetings must be attended by all directors. If a director is unable to attend a board meeting for any reason, he or she may appoint a proxy in writing. Article 26 provided that board meetings shall be held once a year, and interim meetings may be convened upon the proposal of one-third of the directors. Board resolutions in writing and minutes of board meetings shall be signed by all directors present and kept by the company. Article 27 provided that the company shall establish management and operational institutions, including production, technology, sales, finance, and administration departments, and shall have one general manager recommended by Shi Feng Company. The general manager shall implement the resolutions of the board of directors and exercise the company's daily management and operational functions. Zheng Sulan, then legal representative of Shi Feng Company, signed and affixed her seal on the articles of association, and Huang Chongsheng, legal representative of Winning Company, signed the articles of association.

On May 12, 2004, the Taicang Municipal Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation approved the change of shareholders, capital increase, change of board of directors, and amendment of articles of association of Beikelai Company. Beikelai Company completed the corresponding industrial and commercial registration modification procedures. Huang Chongsheng served as chairman of Beikelai Company, Zheng Sulan and Zhang Boqin as directors, and Zhang Boqin was appointed as general manager. Shi Feng Company denied that Zheng Sulan's signature and seal on the articles of association were authentic and claimed it was unaware of the composition of the company's board of directors.

After the completion of the industrial and commercial registration modification procedures for Beikelai Company, Zhang Boqin served as general manager and was responsible for the preparation, construction, production, and operation of Beikelai Company. On August 1, 2004, Yiqiu Metal (Taicang) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yiqiu Company) and Beikelai Company signed a factory lease contract, stipulating that Beikelai Company would lease 4,700 square meters of factory space from Yiqiu Company at a monthly rent of RMB 79,900. A supplementary agreement signed on the same day stipulated that Beikelai Company would pay Yiqiu Company RMB 60,000 per quarter for electricity connection and capacity increase fees for five years, totaling RMB 1.2 million. In October 2004, Beikelai Company officially commenced production and operation, and through a board resolution approved by the Taicang Municipal Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, on November 23, 2004, the company name was changed to Fujun Company upon industrial and commercial registration.

On April 7, 2005, due to disputes between Shi Feng Company and Winning Company over corporate governance structure, patent technology ownership, and related-party transactions, General Manager Zhang Boqin left Fujun Company. Since then, Fujun Company has been managed by Chairman Huang Chongsheng until the present. After Zhang Boqin's departure, to address the management issues of Fujun Company, Shi Feng Company, Winning Company, and Fujun Company exchanged numerous correspondence through their respective lawyers regarding the convening of board meetings. Eventually, on March 31, 2006, the first interim board meeting of Fujun Company was held, attended by Huang Chongsheng and Zhang Boqin (who also represented Zheng Sulan), but no resolution was adopted. Thereafter, Shi Feng Company and Winning Company exchanged written communications regarding Fujun Company's governance issues but failed to reach an agreement, and no further board meeting was convened.

On April 15, 2005, Yiqiu Company filed a lawsuit with the Taicang People's Court of Jiangsu Province, alleging that Fujun Company owed rent, utility fees, and electricity capacity increase fees. On May 9, 2005, the Taicang People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered a civil judgment (2005) Tai Min Yi Chu Zi No. 0745, ordering Fujun Company to pay Yiqiu Company the relevant fees and late payment interest totaling RMB 399,904.73.

On December 18, 2006, as verified by Kunshan Gongxin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., as of March 14, 2005, Fujun Company had paid-in capital of USD 8,899,945, of which Winning Company contributed USD 3.6 million in machinery and equipment, and Shi Feng Company contributed USD 5 million in machinery and equipment and USD 299,945 in cash. Fujun Company's operating performance over the years was as follows: October to December 2004: sales revenue RMB 4.64 million, net profit RMB -1.4 million, depreciation of fixed assets RMB 1.02 million; 2005: sales revenue RMB 6.69 million, net profit RMB -8.33 million, depreciation RMB 7.03 million; 2006: sales revenue RMB 9.09 million, net profit RMB -7.92 million, depreciation RMB 7.01 million; 2007: sales revenue RMB 10.36 million, net profit RMB -6.13 million, depreciation RMB 5.71 million; 2008: sales revenue RMB 7.34 million, net profit RMB -6.27 million, depreciation RMB 5.56 million; 2009: sales revenue RMB 8.04 million, net profit RMB -4.78 million, depreciation RMB -4.46 million; January to June 2010: sales revenue RMB 3.59 million, net profit RMB -3.5 million, depreciation RMB 2.8 million.

On July 28, 2004, COMPOS International Co., Ltd. established a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, Tongyi Company, with Zhang Boqin serving as chairman and general manager. The products produced by Tongyi Company are the same as those of Fujun Company. In March 2008, Fujun Company filed a lawsuit against Zhang Boqin and Tongyi Company with the Jinan Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province for damages for harm to company interests, which has not yet been concluded.

During the trial of this case, the court of first instance conducted multiple rounds of mediation aimed at maintaining the continued existence of Fujun Company. First, it required the three parties to negotiate on improving and restructuring Fujun Company's corporate governance structure, striving to establish a company management and operation method acceptable to all parties. Although the three parties put forward many constructive suggestions, they failed to reach a plan for joint management of the company due to an inability to establish a relationship of trust. Second, it required the three parties to negotiate on the withdrawal of a single shareholder from the company. Because the parties could not agree on the price of the share transfer, they failed to achieve the goal of a single shareholder transferring its shares and withdrawing from the company's management.

The court of first instance held: (1) Regarding the issue of applicable law. Pursuant to Article 14 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, matters such as the civil capacity for rights, civil capacity for conduct, organizational structure, and rights and obligations of shareholders of a legal person and its branches shall be governed by the law of the place of registration. This case concerns a dispute over company dissolution, which is a action for modification filed by a shareholder based on the exercise of shareholder rights. The company sought to be dissolved, Fujun Company, is a foreign-invested enterprise registered in the People's Republic of China, making it a Chinese enterprise legal person. Accordingly, the law of the People's Republic of China, being the place of registration of Fujun Company, should be applied as the governing law for resolving this dispute. Moreover, all parties expressly stated in court that they choose the law of the People's Republic of China, and the parties' intentions are consistent. Therefore, the court determined that the law of the People's Republic of China shall be the governing law for resolving this dispute.

(2) Regarding whether Fujun Company meets the conditions for judicial dissolution under Article 183 of the Company Law. First, Shi Feng Company has the standing to bring a lawsuit for dissolution. Article 183 of the Company Law provides that only a shareholder holding 10% or more of the voting rights of all shareholders of the company has the standing to bring a dissolution lawsuit. In this case, Shi Feng Company holds a 60% equity interest in Fujun Company, and its sole shareholder voting rights exceed 10% of the voting rights of all shareholders.

Second, Fujun Company's management is indeed facing severe difficulties. Severe management difficulties are the first element of a limited liability company falling into a deadlock. The so-called company deadlock refers to a state in the internal governance process of a company where, due to conflicts and tensions between shareholders or between company managers, all decision-making and management mechanisms are paralyzed. The shareholders' meeting or board of directors cannot be convened due to the refusal of the other party to attend, any proposal from one party is not accepted or recognized by the other party, or even if a meeting can be held, no resolution can be adopted due to disagreements among members. In this case, Fujun Company's management has indeed fallen into severe difficulties. First, the board of directors, as the highest authority of Fujun Company, has been unable to perform its functions for a long time. Since Zhang Boqin, the general manager of Fujun Company, left the company on April 7, 2005, only one interim board meeting was held on March 31, 2006, which failed to adopt any resolution. The board of directors has been unable to perform its functions as provided in the articles of association for more than six years. Second, the conflict between the company's directors has remained unresolved for a long time. After Zhang Boqin, the director and general manager of Fujun Company, had disputes with Chairman Huang Chongsheng over corporate governance structure, related-party transactions, etc., and left the company on his own, the three directors of Fujun Company have communicated through correspondence via their lawyers for several years but have failed to reach an agreement to resolve the differences in company management. The conflict has persisted. Furthermore, after Zhang Boqin became the legal representative of Tongyi Company, Fujun Company filed a lawsuit against Zhang Boqin for damages for harm to company interests, which escalated the conflicts among the parties. Third, the company management model stipulated in the articles of association has become a mere formality. According to Fujun Company's articles of association, the general manager implements the resolutions of the board of directors and exercises the company's daily management and operational functions. As the employed general manager of Fujun Company, Zhang Boqin has not engaged in company management for a long time. The company has been managed solely by the chairman appointed by one shareholder, rendering the corporate governance structure established by the articles of association a mere formality.

Third, the continued existence of the company will cause significant harm to the shareholders' rights and interests. On the one hand, from the perspective of Fujun Company's operating performance, the shareholders' investment has not yielded returns for a long time. Since its establishment, Fujun Company has been in a loss-making position. Although under Huang Chongsheng's six-year unilateral management, the company's losses have been decreasing year by year, it has never turned around to profitability, causing significant economic losses to the shareholders. On the other hand, from the perspective of Fujun Company's management, the modern corporate governance structure has failed to function effectively. Due to the unresolved conflict between the two shareholders, Fujun Company has been managed unilaterally by the chairman appointed by Winning Company. As the major shareholder, Shi Feng Company has been excluded from the company and has been unable to exercise appropriate participation in the company's operation, decision-making, management, and supervision rights based on its investment, resulting in significant harm to its shareholder rights and interests.

Fourth, all efforts to resolve the deadlock through various means have failed. After conflicts arose among the shareholders of Fujun Company, both shareholder parties attempted to resolve the disputes through multiple channels but all proved unsuccessful. On the one hand, the shareholders themselves engaged in communication and coordination. Both shareholder parties retained lawyers to participate in handling the disputes, and over a period of more than two years, exchanged more than ten rounds of correspondence and held one interim board meeting, yet failed to reach a consensus on the disputed issues. On the other hand, after the lawsuit was filed, under the auspices of the People's Court, the three parties conducted multiple rounds of mediation, from reestablishing a new corporate governance structure for Fujun Company to the unilateral exit of a shareholder via equity transfer. Each shareholder party proposed solutions, but none resulted in a mutually agreed mediation agreement.

Fifth, the defenses raised by Fujun Company and Yongli Company cannot be sustained. 1. Regarding the defense that the conflict between the shareholders was caused by Shifeng Company and that Fujun Company should not be dissolved. A limited liability company, in addition to its capital-based nature, also has a strong personal nature. Shareholders are typically both investors and managers of the company, and the trust and cooperation among shareholders are important foundations for the normal operation of the company. Since the emergence of the limited liability company system, to ensure the stable operation of the company, the company has always operated under the principle of capital democracy through "majority voting of shares." When the trust between shareholders is lost and a corporate deadlock arises, one shareholder controls the company's operational rights and property rights, imposing de facto coercion and serious unfairness on the other shareholders, effectively depriving the latter of their lawful rights to management based on their invested shares. This situation constitutes one of the conditions for judicial dissolution of the company. The deadlock in Fujun Company began on April 7, 2005, when Zhang Boqin left the company. The cause was that after the shareholder parties diverged on issues such as the arrangement of the company's governance structure, patent ownership, and related-party transactions, the basis of trust for jointly managing the company was gradually lost, leading to the corporate deadlock. Shifeng Company alleged that Yongli Company forged a board resolution to amend the articles of association, thereby taking the position of chairman of Fujun Company, claiming that the signature and seal on the articles of association were not those of its legal representative. However, after the amendment of the articles of association, Zhang Boqin, appointed by Shifeng Company, served as the general manager of Beikelai Company for a long period, responsible for operations and management, and the articles were amended to change the company name to Fujun Company. Therefore, Shifeng Company's unilateral denial is insufficient to prove that Yongli Company forged the board resolution to amend the articles of association. Although the reasons for Shifeng Company's loss of trust in Yongli Company may not necessarily be valid, whether the company should be dissolved depends on the existence of a deadlock, not on the cause or fault leading to the deadlock. Accordingly, the defenses of Fujun Company and Yongli Company that dissolution should not be allowed because the conflict was caused by Shifeng Company lack legal basis, and this court does not accept them. 2. Regarding the defense that Shifeng Company brought this lawsuit in bad faith, seeking to monopolize the market, and therefore the company should not be dissolved. Tongyi Company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established by COMPOS International Co., Ltd., and Fujun Company and Yongli Company failed to provide evidence proving an affiliated relationship between Tongyi Company and Shifeng Company. Although Zhang Boqin was a director appointed by Shifeng Company to Fujun Company, in the absence of corroborating evidence, Zhang Boqin's appointment as chairman of Tongyi Company cannot be automatically deemed as representing Shifeng Company. Therefore, the defense of Fujun Company and Yongli Company that Shifeng Company brought this lawsuit in bad faith to monopolize the market lacks factual basis, and this court does not accept it. As for whether Zhang Boqin, as a senior manager of Fujun Company, should bear liability for harming the company's rights and interests, that issue should be dealt with in the case of Fujun Company v. Zhang Boqin and Tongyi Company regarding compensation for damage to company interests; this case does not address it. Even if the judgment in this case dissolves Fujun Company, it does not affect the company's standing as a litigant in that case.

In summary, Fujun Company has experienced severe difficulties in its operations and management, its continued existence would cause significant losses to the shareholders' interests, and no other means can resolve the issues. Therefore, the request of Shifeng Company, which holds 60% of all shareholders' voting rights, to dissolve Fujun Company is granted in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 14 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 183 and 218 of the Company Law, and Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II) (hereinafter referred to as the "Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law"), this court orders the dissolution of Fujun Company. The litigation costs at first instance, RMB 422,865, shall be borne by Fujun Company.

Fujun Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this court, arguing as follows: (1) The original judgment erred in finding the facts. A. The original judgment incorrectly found the reason for Zhang Boqin, the director and general manager appointed by Shifeng Company, leaving Fujun Company. Zhang Boqin left Fujun Company on April 7, 2005, the real reason being that he violated the duty of loyalty and non-compete obligations of senior company management by serving as the legal representative and executive director of Tongyi Company, producing and selling products identical to those of Fujun Company, encroaching on Fujun Company's market, and harming Fujun Company's interests. There was no dispute between Yongli Company and Shifeng Company over the company's governance structure, nor were there disputes over patent technology ownership, related-party transactions, or similar issues. B. Fujun Company has not experienced severe difficulties in its operations and management. Fujun Company's product, building panels, is an environmentally friendly product just emerging in mainland China with promising market prospects. Fujun Company's turnover has been expanding year by year. The financial statements reflect losses due to overvaluation of machinery and equipment and significant depreciation amounts. Currently, the company's operations and management are in good order, losses are decreasing year by year, and the company is transitioning toward turning losses into profits. C. The deadlock in Fujun Company's board of directors was unilaterally and artificially created by Shifeng Company. After Zhang Boqin left Fujun Company without authorization, upon receiving notice of a board meeting of Fujun Company, he intentionally failed to attend, manufacturing a corporate deadlock. Shifeng Company's purpose in seeking dissolution through judicial means is to cause Fujun Company to cease to exist and thereby monopolize the market share. (2) The original judgment erred in applying the law. The legislative purpose of Article 183 of the Company Law is to provide a last-resort remedy for innocent and aggrieved parties in a corporate deadlock situation. If a shareholder at fault for creating the deadlock is allowed to dissolve the company through litigation, it would cause secondary harm to innocent shareholders, contravening the legislative intent of that article. Shifeng Company could choose to reappoint directors, appoint a general manager to continue the joint venture operations, negotiate equity transfer to initiate an exit mechanism, or determine the company's ownership through bidding, yet it only selected dissolution, which would cause damage to the shareholders' interests of Fujun Company, idle equipment, employee layoffs, and is detrimental to resource efficiency and social stability. Shifeng Company's abuse of rights and malicious litigation should not be supported. Fujun Company requested this court to set aside the original judgment and instead dismiss all of Shifeng Company's claims.

Shifeng Company responded, arguing: (1) The original judgment found the facts clearly. Since April 2005, Fujun Company has experienced long-term conflicts among directors, with no shareholders' meetings or board meetings able to be convened for over six years, and no effective shareholders' meeting or board resolutions have been formed, resulting in severe difficulties in the company's operations. After Yongli Company completely controlled Fujun Company independently from 2005, the company's operating condition deteriorated steadily, with severe losses and continuous significant damage to the shareholders' interests. (2) The original judgment correctly applied the law. After the disputes arose, the shareholders of Fujun Company, through their appointed directors and lawyers, explored solutions for one party to exit. The court of first instance also conducted multiple rounds of mediation at various levels, but due to the shareholders' animosity and differences, no agreement could be reached. The dissolution ordered by the original judgment was made with caution. The potential consequences of dissolution, such as employee dismissals and reemployment, can be addressed through legal remedies under the Company Law, Labor Law, and other laws, and cannot serve as a reason to maintain the current status. In summary, Shifeng Company requested this court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Yongli Company stated: It agrees with Fujun Company's arguments.

During the second-instance proceedings, Fujun Company submitted the Civil Judgment No. 19 (2008), Fourth Commercial Division, Jinan Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province and the Civil Judgment No. 181 (2011), Fourth Commercial Division, Shandong High People's Court. All parties confirmed the authenticity of these judgments, and this court acknowledges them.

The facts found by the original judgment are confirmed as correct by this court.

This court further finds: On July 6, 2011, the Jinan Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province rendered Civil Judgment No. 19 (2008), Fourth Commercial Division, in the case of Fujun Company v. Zhang Boqin and Tongyi Company concerning damage to company rights and interests, finding that the main products of Tongyi Company were the same as those of Fujun Company, constituting competing business. Zhang Boqin, as a senior manager of Fujun Company, served as executive director, legal representative, and general manager of Tongyi Company, which violated his duty of non-compete to Fujun Company, and Fujun Company was entitled to exercise its right of disgorgement. The judgment ordered: 1. Zhang Boqin and Tongyi Company shall, within two months after the judgment takes effect, complete the registration change with the administrative authority for industry and commerce to remove Zhang Boqin from his positions as executive director, legal representative, and general manager of Tongyi Company; 2. Zhang Boqin shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, compensate Fujun Company for economic losses of RMB 100,000; 3. All other claims of Fujun Company were dismissed. Zhang Boqin appealed the judgment to the Shandong High People's Court, which rendered Civil Judgment No. 181 (2011), Fourth Commercial Division, on February 24, 2012, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

It is further found: Yongli Company and Shifeng Company did not enter into a joint venture contract but signed the articles of association of Fujun Company. Article 18 of the articles of association provides: "The board of directors decides all major issues of the company, with its main authorities as follows: 1. Amendment of the articles of association; 2. Suspension, dissolution, or merger of the company with other economic organizations; 3. Increase or decrease of the registered capital of the company, transfer of all or part of the company's assets, increase and transfer of equity, and other major resolutions of the company, which shall be amended only with the consent of both Yongli Company and Shifeng Company; 4. Decisions on annual production plans, sales plans, and development plans; 5. Approval of annual financial budgets, final accounts, and accounting reports; 6. Methods for handling annual financial budget profits and losses; 7. Discussion and adoption of important internal rules and regulations; 8. Review and approval of the general manager's annual operating report; 9. Deliberation and resolution of proposals submitted by the general manager; 10. Appointment and removal of the general manager and other senior staff at the manager level and above; 11. Responsibility for liquidation upon termination or expiration of the company." Article 19 provides: "The contents of the various clauses in Article 18 shall take effect only with the consent of all directors."

During the second-instance proceedings, this court conducted multiple rounds of mediation aimed at preserving the existence of Fujun Company. Given that Yongli Company and Shifeng Company had lost the basis of trust for jointly managing the company, the mediation primarily focused on negotiating a plan for one shareholder to exit Fujun Company. During mediation, Fujun Company submitted its balance sheet as of October 31, 2011, showing paid-in capital of RMB 76,972,153.35, accumulated losses of RMB -40,814,925.41, shareholders' equity at the beginning of the year of RMB 36,157,227.94, and shareholders' equity at the end of the period of RMB 31,909,051.91. Based on the balance sheet information disclosed by Fujun Company, Shifeng Company and Yongli Company agreed that Shifeng Company would acquire the 40% equity held by Yongli Company, and they largely reached a consensus on the equity transfer price. However, because the two shareholder parties could not reach an agreement on specific terms of the mediation agreement, including whether Fujun Company should fully disclose its financial and operational information to Shifeng Company before the equity acquisition and whether Yongli Company should assume a guarantee liability for any debts of Fujun Company not reflected in the disclosed balance sheet, they ultimately failed to conclude a mediation agreement to preserve Fujun Company's existence.

This court holds that this case is a dispute over the dissolution of a company. Fujun Company, the company sought to be dissolved, is a foreign-invested enterprise established in the form of a limited liability company within the territory of the People's Republic of China by two foreign investors. Pursuant to Article 2 and Article 218 of the Company Law, disputes over the dissolution of a company established in China shall be governed by Chinese law. All parties have no objection to the application of Chinese law to resolve the dispute in this case, and this court confirms that. Since the Law of the People's Republic of China on Foreign-Capital Enterprises and its implementing rules do not provide specific provisions on circumstances where shareholders may petition the People's Court for dissolution of a company, according to Article 218 of the Company Law, which states that "limited liability companies and companies limited by shares with foreign investment shall be governed by this Law," this case shall examine whether Shifeng Company's request to dissolve Fujun Company can be upheld in accordance with Article 183 of the Company Law and the Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law.

Article 183 of the Company Law provides: "Where a company experiences severe difficulties in its operations and management, the continued existence of which would cause significant losses to the shareholders' interests, and such difficulties cannot be resolved through other means, a shareholder holding 10% or more of all shareholders' voting rights may petition the People's Court for dissolution of the company." Paragraph 1 of Article 1 of the Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law provides: "A shareholder who individually or jointly holds 10% or more of all shareholders' voting rights of a company, filing a lawsuit for dissolution of the company on any of the following grounds, and meeting the conditions set forth in Article 183 of the Company Law, shall be accepted by the People's Court: (1) The company has been unable to convene a shareholders' meeting or shareholders' general meeting for more than two consecutive years, and the company's operations and management have experienced severe difficulties; (2) Shareholders fail to reach the required quorum or voting ratio as stipulated by laws or the articles of association, and have been unable to make effective shareholders' meeting or shareholders' general meeting resolutions for more than two consecutive years, and the company's operations and management have experienced severe difficulties; (3) There is a long-term conflict among the company's directors that cannot be resolved through the shareholders' meeting or shareholders' general meeting, and the company's operations and management have experienced severe difficulties; (4) Other circumstances where severe difficulties in operations and management arise, and the continued existence of the company would cause significant losses to the shareholders' interests." The above provisions serve not only as the conditions for accepting a dissolution lawsuit but also as the substantive criteria for adjudicating the dissolution of a company.

First, whether Fujun Company has experienced severe difficulties in its operations and management. Severe difficulties in the operations and management of a company include two situations: first, severe difficulties in the operation of corporate powers, where the shareholders' meeting, board of directors, and other decision-making and management bodies cannot function normally and cannot make any resolutions on any matters of the company, i.e., a corporate deadlock; second, severe difficulties in the company's business operations, such as poor management and serious losses. If a company only experiences severe difficulties in its business operations but not in the operation of its corporate powers, pursuant to paragraph 2 of Article 1 of the Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law, it does not satisfy the conditions for dissolution under Article 183 of the Company Law.

In this case, according to Articles 17 and 21 of Fujun Company's articles of association, the board of directors of Fujun Company is the highest authority of the company. Both Shifeng Company and Yongli Company manage Fujun Company by appointing directors, i.e., the board of directors directly exercises the dual functions of the board of directors and the shareholders' meeting. At the same time, according to Article 19 of the articles of association, matters such as production and sales plans, financial budgets and final accounts plans, methods for handling financial profits and losses, and appointment and removal of senior staff at the manager level and above require the consent of all directors to take effect. The strict unanimous voting mechanism agreed upon by the shareholders in Fujun Company's governance structure makes the personal nature the most important characteristic of Fujun Company. Since April 2005, Yongli Company and Shifeng Company have had substantive differences over issues such as the lease of Fujun Company's factory premises, the arrangement of the company's governance structure, and the licensing of patents. The trust and cooperation foundation between the shareholders has gradually been lost. Not only has the board of directors of Fujun Company been in a state of being unable to convene for a long period, but even at the only interim board meeting convened with the coordination of the respective lawyers of Yongli Company and Shifeng Company, due to significant disagreements between the two shareholder parties, it was impossible to form a board resolution in accordance with the voting ratio requirements stipulated in the articles of association. The decision-making mechanism of Fujun Company has been long-term dysfunctional, unable to operate for a period of seven years, which constitutes a corporate deadlock situation of severe difficulties in operations and management as provided in Items (1) and (2) of Article 1 of the Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law.

Second, whether the cause and fault for the corporate deadlock should be considered when dissolving the company. Fujun Company appealed, arguing that Zhang Boqin, the director appointed by Shifeng Company, left his post without authorization, failed to attend board meetings, artificially created a corporate deadlock, and harmed the interests of Fujun Company, and therefore the court should not support the litigation brought by Shifeng Company with malicious intent. Shifeng Company argued in defense that Yongli Company obtained the position of chairman through fraud, leading to the deadlock. This court holds that whether a company can be dissolved depends on the existence of a corporate deadlock and whether the substantive conditions set forth in Article 183 of the Company Law are met, not on the cause or fault for the deadlock. Article 183 of the Company Law does not restrict a shareholder at fault from petitioning for dissolution of the company. Therefore, even if one shareholder is at fault for the creation of the corporate deadlock, it still has the right to petition for dissolution of the company under that article. In this case, the background for Shifeng Company's request to dissolve Fujun Company is that Fujun Company has been in a corporate deadlock and under the unilateral management of Yongli Company for seven years. Shifeng Company holds 60% of the shares, and its exercise of the right to petition for judicial dissolution meets the requirements of Article 183 of the Company Law and does not constitute an abuse of rights or malicious litigation. As for whether Zhang Boqin, the director appointed by Shifeng Company, committed a wrongful act in breach of his duty of non-compete as a director and whether he should bear civil liability for compensating Fujun Company's losses, that issue shall be resolved by Fujun Company in a separate case and is not related to this case.

Third, whether the continued existence of Fujun Company would cause significant losses to the shareholders' interests. From the perspective of Fujun Company's operations, after the corporate deadlock formed, the company's operations fell into an abnormal mode. During the period of unilateral management by Yongli Company, although Fujun Company's business did not cease, it incurred continuous losses, had no profitable year, and its operational capacity and debt repayment ability significantly weakened. The shareholders' equity has been substantially reduced to less than half of the paid-in capital. Fujun Company's argument on appeal that its production and operations are normal, losses are decreasing, and it is expected to turn losses into profits lacks sufficient evidentiary support, and this court does not accept it. Additionally, from the perspective of the capital contribution to Fujun Company, neither Shifeng Company nor Yongli Company has fully paid in their capital contributions to date. Given that both shareholder parties are unwilling to jointly manage Fujun Company and their conflicts and antagonism cannot be reconciled, it is difficult to replenish Fujun Company's registered capital and achieve the intended business objectives. Considering the above circumstances, Fujun Company has not only lost its personal foundation, with severe difficulties in the operation of its corporate powers, but its business operations are also in a state of severe difficulty. The continued existence of the company would cause significant losses to the shareholders' interests.

Fourth, regarding the feasibility of alternative remedies. Article 5, paragraph 1 of the Judicial Interpretation (II) of the Company Law provides: "When hearing a lawsuit for dissolution of a company, the people's court shall emphasize mediation. If the parties, through consultation, agree that the company or its shareholders shall purchase shares, or that the company shall continue to exist through capital reduction or other means, and such agreement does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, the people's court shall support it. If the parties cannot reach a consensus to maintain the company's existence, the people's court shall render a judgment in a timely manner." A company deadlock does not inevitably lead to dissolution; the judiciary should exercise caution in intervening in corporate affairs. Wherever there are other means to maintain the company's existence, the company should not be readily dissolved. However, in this case, after multiple rounds of mediation by the courts of first and second instance, Yongli Company and Shifeng Company were consistently unable to reach an agreement on solutions to maintain the existence of Fujun Company, such as transferring equity, company buyback, or capital reduction. Especially during the mediation in the second instance, Shifeng Company was willing to acquire Yongli Company's equity to keep Fujun Company existing, and the two parties had basically reached an agreement on the equity transfer price. However, because Fujun Company was unwilling to fully disclose its business conditions and external debts during the period of Yongli Company's unilateral management, a mediation agreement was ultimately not reached. The Company Law does not establish other alternative remedies to resolve a company deadlock. Currently, the persistent deadlock of Fujun Company has exhausted other means and remains unresolved. If Fujun Company is maintained, shareholders' rights and interests will only be gradually depleted in the stalemate. By comparison, dissolving Fujun Company can provide an exit mechanism for both shareholders and avoid irreparable major losses to shareholders' interests.

In summary, the management and operations of Fujun Company have encountered serious difficulties, and continued existence will cause significant losses to shareholders' interests, and the situation cannot be resolved through other means. Shifeng Company, as the shareholder holding 60% of the shares, filed a request to dissolve Fujun Company, which complies with the provisions of Article 183 of the Company Law and should be granted. Fujun Company's grounds for appeal cannot be established and should be dismissed. The original judgment found clear facts, correctly applied the law, and the result was not improper, and should be affirmed. This Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby renders the following judgment:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 422,865 shall be borne by Fujun New Composite Materials (Taicang) Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
